goals.title: Help newcomers take a confident first step
Give creators useful foundations to Riff

entries.question: What can someone actually see in a blockchain transaction?
entries.title: What can you see?
entries.observation: New Lore publishes a question about transaction visibility. This is a learning prompt, not evidence of search volume.
entries.build: Make a tiny interactive scene where a player switches between sender, recipient and observer views. Show what each role can see using clearly labeled simulated data.
entries.success: A first-time visitor can explain which information is visible in your example. Include a source note and one editable scenario.

entries.question: How can a newcomer understand XTM on Tari L1 and TARI on Tari L2?
entries.title: One confident next step
entries.observation: The linked New Lore page uses an outdated L2 token name in its URL and may use it in its content. TARI is the canonical L2 token name, confirmed by the project owner on 2026-09-23. Use the question as inspiration; validate any actual flow against current protocol documentation.
entries.build: Create a reusable onboarding design kit: an illustrated L1/L2 concept map labeled XTM and TARI, a simulated confirmation screen and a recovery/help state. Explain each term before asking for an action; do not assume a conversion mechanism is implemented.
entries.success: Someone new to Tari can describe the proposed action and its limits. Include editable components; do not connect a real wallet for this first prototype.

entries.question: What does mining on a laptop involve?
entries.title: Teach it in one playable minute
entries.observation: New Lore publishes laptop-mining questions. A hands-on teaching exercise could help explain choices without promising earnings.
entries.build: Riff a small game into a one-minute mining concept simulator. Let the player change one variable, observe a clear result, and open a short explanation. Label all numbers as illustrative.
entries.success: The player can explain the changed variable after one round. Publish the editable rules, a working demo and a short walkthrough; no profitability forecasts.

entries.question: What does an audit result establish—and what remains unknown?
entries.title: Read the evidence
entries.observation: New Lore has an audit-literacy question. Turn the question into a reusable evidence-reading exercise, not a security endorsement.
entries.build: Build an interactive card exercise matching audit scope, severity, remediation and date to their meanings. Use fictional examples and link to primary evidence for any real claim.
entries.success: A learner can distinguish a checked claim from an untested assumption. Include an editable lesson and a three-question knowledge check.
